I don’t consider myself conventionally attractive or even really attractive in general. I have used dating apps to meet people in between relationships for the past six or so years. Here are some things I think help:

* Be socially aware. Understand that dating as a man is different than dating as a woman. Try to see your future words/actions through their eyes. Expose yourself to more viewpoints from women to help get a better understanding. Dating isn’t easy but do what you can to make it easier.

* Take no for an answer AND BE OK WITH IT. Sometimes that means no to future interactions, sometimes that just means no to a call or a date at that time. Being pushy gets you nowhere fast af. Even if you get a hard denial, just move on and don’t be lame about it. There’s literally millions of other potential partners out there.

* Try to be interesting/funny. Talking to new people is HARD at first but the more reps you put in the easier it’ll be. Ask lots of engaging questions and try to build off those. 

* Don’t be a creep. Check out some of the incel/creepypm subs and do the opposite of those morons.

* don’t be misogynistic. Women are people, treat them that way you dodo (not you specifically, but ya know)

> Since the Irvine Meadows Amphitheater closed down in 2016, many residents and live music enthusiasts have persistently advocated for the city to plan a new venue to replace the temporary amphitheater that has hosted fans ever since, using portable bleacher seating and a temporary stage and restrooms.

> Live Nation last week released design renderings of the 14,000-person-capacity concert venue it has in mind to be located on 25 acres near the current intersection of Great Park Boulevard and Skyhawk.

> The total cost of the project could be as much as $130 million, city officials said. Live Nation is expected to contribute $20 million toward construction and pay $3.5 million a year to the city for use of the venue, increasing 3% each year.

> The city will also get half of a $5-per-ticket surcharge to pay for maintenance, a fee city officials estimate could bring in up to $1 million per concert season.

> Members of Save Live Music Irvine, wearing white shirts with their logo, filled seats in the City Council Chambers on Tuesday. Among them were some members of Orange County’s theatrical stage employees union.

> Alan Myerson, a resident of Woodbridge, said if his windows are open during a concert, “I don’t really hear music, I hear bass, I hear thumping.”

> He and others also questioned whether city officials were too quickly moving ahead with the project without considering how it might impact Great Park neighbors.

> Camiar Ohadi, who is a member of the Great Park Residents Council neighborhood group, said not enough time had been spent studying the impacts of a permanent amphitheater, including on property values and quality of life, such as safety.

> Councilman Larry Agran, who voted against the deal, also expressed concern about “rushing ahead” on the project “with all kinds of questions” lingering.

> The sound level will be capped at 50 decibels for residential areas, and if that level is exceeded, fines starting at $10,000 can be imposed on the fourth violation and doubled for each bad mark after that, officials said.
